title: Implement wildcard pattern matching where '?' matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters including the empty sequence.

s1_definition.profdef: 2D DP where dp[i][j] means the first i chars of text match the first j chars of pattern. For '*': dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j] (star absorbs one more text char) OR dp[i][j−1] (star matches empty). For '?' or an exact char: dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] when the single char matches. Time O(m·n), space O(n).
s1_definition.analogy: A file-name matcher at National Bank of India filters statement files by a glob pattern. A question mark matches exactly one character and a star matches any run of characters, so at a star the matcher can either swallow one more character or declare the star finished.
s1_definition.oneliner: '*' = extend over one more char OR match empty; '?'/char = diagonal when single matches.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** 2D DP where dp[i][j] means the first i chars of text match the first j chars of pattern. For '*': dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j] (star absorbs one more text char) OR dp[i][j−1] (star matches empty). For '?' or an exact char: dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] when the single char matches. Time O(m·n), space O(n).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A file-name matcher at National Bank of India filters statement files by a glob pattern. A question mark matches exactly one character and a star matches any run of characters, so at a star the matcher can either swallow one more character or declare the star finished.

**One line to remember:** '*' = extend over one more char OR match empty; '?'/char = diagonal when single matches.

sections.s2_technical:
This is simpler than full regex because the star here is standalone, matching any sequence directly, not tied to a preceding element. Build dp of size (m+1) by (n+1). dp[0][0] is true, and the first row is true for a leading run of stars because each star can match the empty text: dp[0][j] = dp[0][j−1] when the pattern char is a star.

For the body, if the pattern char is a star, dp[i][j] is true if the star matches the current text char and continues, which is dp[i−1][j], or the star matches empty, which is dp[i][j−1]. For example: `if (pc=='*') dp[i][j]=dp[i-1][j] || dp[i][j-1];`. If the pattern char is a question mark or equals the text char, inherit the diagonal: `else if (pc=='?' || pc==s.charAt(i-1)) dp[i][j]=dp[i-1][j-1];`. Otherwise it stays false. The answer is dp[m][n].

The time is O(m·n), space reduces to O(n). A senior nuance is that a greedy two-pointer solution with a backtrack position for the last star also solves this in O(m·n) worst case but O(1) space, which is a strong follow-up answer.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a batch processor filters statement file names by a glob pattern where a question mark matches one character and a star matches any run. This is exactly how Wildcard Matching works.

Problem 2 — A star can match nothing or a long stretch, so a plain scan cannot decide where the star should stop. This is exactly why the DP encodes both the match-one-more and match-empty branches.

The mini-project builds a `FileNameMatcher`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input text is adceb and the pattern is star a star b.

Step 1: dp of zero and zero is true, and the leading star makes dp of zero and one true because a star can match empty.

Step 2: The first star absorbs the leading characters up to a, keeping true states flowing rightward and downward.

Step 3: The a in the pattern matches the a in the text via the diagonal.

Step 4: The second star absorbs d, c, e, and the final b matches the b in the text.

Step 5: The bottom-right cell is true so the first case matches, while a-star-c-question-b fails to cover acdcb and ends false.

```text
2026-10-27T04:40:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — File Name Matcher (Wildcard Matching)
2026-10-27T04:40:00Z [INFO] isMatch(adceb,*a*b) = true
2026-10-27T04:40:00Z [INFO] 'adceb' vs '*a*b' → true
2026-10-27T04:40:00Z [INFO] isMatch(acdcb,a*c?b) = false
2026-10-27T04:40:00Z [INFO] 'acdcb' vs 'a*c?b' → false
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  s=adceb  p=*a*b
  dp[0][0]=T ; leading '*' → dp[0][1]=T
  '*': dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] (consume one more) || dp[i][j-1] (match empty)
  '?'/char: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] when single matches
  dp[m][n] = true
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Wildcard Matching is a two-dimensional dynamic programming problem that is simpler than full regular expression matching because the star here is standalone and matches any sequence directly, rather than being tied to a preceding element. I define dp of i and j as whether the first i characters of the text match the first j characters of the pattern. The empty-empty cell is true, and I make the first row true across a leading run of stars because each star can match the empty text.

The body has two cases. If the pattern character is a star, the cell is true if the star absorbs one more text character, which is the cell above, or the star matches empty, which is the cell to the left. If the pattern character is a question mark or exactly equals the text character, I inherit the diagonal. Otherwise the cell stays false, and the answer is the bottom-right cell.

In my project at National Bank of India, a batch processor filtered statement file names by a glob pattern where a question mark matched one character and a star matched any run. Because a star can match nothing or a long stretch, a plain scan cannot decide where it should stop, so I used this DP, and I mention the greedy two-pointer variant with a saved star position as a constant-space follow-up.
